title: Choose the visual world for TempoDojo
question: The roll assigned Screenprint Gig Poster. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Screenprint Gig Poster
options.lineage: two-ink screenprinted club and gig posters
options.thesis: Every practice session pulled like a two-ink gig poster on black stock.
options.viewport: A giant condensed BPM headline, a row of beat blocks like poster dates, thumb transport and tabs below.
options.risk: Misregistration reads as a rendering bug if it is used for anything but the downbeat.

raised.raise: Orange ink is reserved for 'now' alone: the live downbeat and Play. Nothing else is ever orange.
A head line always names where you are: bar, beat and session time, recomputed live.
Beat blocks repack in whole cells at every width; they never squeeze or wrap mid-bar.

options.label: Stick Control Page
options.lineage: George Lawrence Stone's Stick Control method book
options.thesis: The metronome typeset as a drill page: numbered exercises, sticking in rows.
options.viewport: Exercise number and BPM set as a page heading, the beat row as an R/L sticking line with the live note circled.
options.risk: The direction most drummer apps would reach for; a light page glares under dim practice-room light.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Beats as spectral lines on one rail; accent, normal, ghost and mute told by line height and dash.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail carrying a line per beat, the BPM as a bone legend above it.
options.case: Fuses well: accent levels map exactly to line form. Loses on audience identification, since this is astronomy, not drumming.
options.risk: Hairlines are hard to read from the throne at 2 m.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Practice sessions as sides of a mixtape: timed, labelled, flipped.
options.viewport: BPM in block caps, presets as a side-A tracklist, the practice timer as a tape counter.
options.case: Fuses: presets map to a tracklist and the timer to a tape side. Loses on clarity, since hand lettering does not read from 2 m.
options.risk: Handwriting at stand distance is illegible.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: A calm, friendly practice app where the one bright colour is always something you can press.
options.viewport: Stacked cards for tempo, beats and timer, with a thumb bar at the bottom.
options.case: Holds product clarity. Loses on audience identification, since it could be any habit app.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Practice as a course of controls over fixed terrain.
options.viewport: A course line from control to control.
options.case: Fuses poorly: drummers do not identify with orienteering, and a map obscures a metronome.
options.kept: One ink reserved strictly for the live leg.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Entries ranked by apparatus, guide words at the head.
options.viewport: A column of entries under guide words.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reading page fights a live, glanceable instrument.
options.kept: Guide words that name exactly where you are.
options.risk: Too small to read from the throne.

options.label: Doujin Event Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-sized cells in a numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: A packed grid of numbered cells.
options.case: Fuses poorly: density is the opposite of a glanceable metronome.
options.kept: Cells repack in whole units, never squeezed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What metronome apps like Tempo ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A big BPM, beat dots, and a play button, at full craft.
